narrative: Every reviewer premise in this PR held up, and the agent accepted or redirected every finding correctly, often with stronger fixes than proposed (four-valued blockerKind, hoisting the per-step rules). The cost came from fixes that were too narrow. Comment and doc corrections were applied to the quoted instance and not to siblings (F7, F8, F14, F18, F23), and F20's bool partition of the exhaustion message introduced a new false claim, "claimed by another checkout", for out-of-view and not-ready blockers (F21, F22, F27). Round 3 still contained one pre-existing finding (F24), but round 4's three findings were all caused by fixes, and the round-5 push (capped, unreviewed) existed only to fix those.
guidance_observations: The agent restated the same eligibility and announcement rules in each step of the design doc, the code comments, and the CHANGELOG, and each round found one more drifted copy; hoisting on the first such finding (as finally done for F19) would have cut two rounds.
Fixes to diagnostic wording replaced one uniform message with a bool split without first enumerating every reason the predicate could be false, which turned a known lie into a new one.
The agent's mutation-verification of new tests caught its own vacuous negative assertion (3d5955d vs efe5eaa); that habit should run before the fix is pushed, not after.
The round cap left 644ad23 unreviewed; the round-4 fixes are doc-only, but nothing reviewed them.
